title: "Rising F mean curves: recovery study"
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: true
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, fig.path = "results/f_mean_curves/figures/"
)
attempts <- readRDS("results/f_mean_curves/recovery.rds")
groups <- vapply(attempts, function(a) paste(a$kind, a$curve, a$process, a$stress), character(1))
```

## What was tested

`mono(age)` describes a flexible non-decreasing mean F, including exact plateaus.
`logistic(age)` describes a smooth rising mean that approaches an estimated
asymptote. Realized F fluctuates around either mean, with IID or separable AR1
residuals. These curves constrain the mean, rather than each annual F profile.

There are 100 isolated Gaussian replicates and 30 full-population replicates
for each of the four curve/process combinations. Each stress case adds 20
replicates at both levels. The mono stress has four exact zero increments;
the logistic stress places its midpoint at the youngest observed age, limiting
information below the midpoint. Full assessments have 30 years, eight ages,
two surveys, fixed M and observation log-SDs of 0.08. All attempts and warnings
are retained. Fits are not retried or simplified.

## Numerical success

```{r}
summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(groups), function(group) {
  a <- attempts[groups == group]
  data.frame(
    Design = group, Attempts = length(a),
    Passed = sum(vapply(a, function(x) isTRUE(x$numerical), logical(1))),
    Errors = sum(vapply(a, function(x) !is.null(x$error), logical(1))),
    `Positive Hessian` = sum(vapply(a, function(x) isTRUE(x$pdHess), logical(1))), check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(summary)
```

Numerical convergence requires optimizer success, a positive-definite Hessian
and a sufficiently small gradient. Mono uses the gradient appropriate to its
zero bounds. These checks do not establish statistical support for the curve.

## Curve and parameter recovery

```{r}
recovery <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(attempts), function(name) {
  a <- attempts[[name]]
  if (is.null(a$recovery)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  transform(a$recovery, design = groups[[name]], numerical = isTRUE(a$numerical))
}))
recovery$bias <- recovery$estimate - recovery$truth
tab <- aggregate(covered ~ design, recovery, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
names(tab)[2] <- "Parameter coverage"
knitr::kable(tab, digits = 3)
```

Coverage is reported for all attempts with available uncertainty, including
those failing numerical checks. Boundary Wald intervals for mono are local
approximations. Their coverage must not be interpreted as boundary-adjusted
inference. The detailed results retain parameter bias and uncertainty on each
parameter's fitted scale; midpoints, log slopes and log-F increments are not
averaged together.

```{r}
full <- Filter(function(a) a$kind == "full" && !is.null(a$curve_rmse), attempts)
if (length(full)) {
  labels <- vapply(full, function(a) paste(a$curve, a$process, a$stress), character(1))
  rmse <- vapply(full, `[[`, numeric(1), "curve_rmse")
  par(mar = c(8, 4, 1, 1))
  boxplot(split(rmse, labels), las = 2, ylab = "Mean-F curve RMSE (per year)", col = "grey85")
}
```

```{r profiles}
paths <- list.files("results/f_mean_curves", "^full_.*none_1[.]rds$", full.names = TRUE)
if (length(paths)) {
  par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
  for (path in paths) {
    fit <- readRDS(path)
    curve <- if (grepl("mono", path)) "mono" else "logistic"
    profile <- subset(tinyAM::tidy_pop(fit)$mu_F, year == min(fit$dat$years))
    truth <- if (curve == "mono") {
      .08 * exp(c(0, cumsum(c(.7, .5, .3, .15, .1, .05, .05))))
    } else {
      .5 * plogis(1.1 * (profile$age - 4.5))
    }
    plot(profile$age, profile$est,
      type = "l", xlab = "Age", ylab = "Mean F",
      ylim = range(c(truth, profile$lwr, profile$upr), finite = TRUE),
      main = paste(curve, fit$dat$F_settings$process)
    )
    polygon(c(profile$age, rev(profile$age)), c(profile$lwr, rev(profile$upr)),
      col = adjustcolor("steelblue", .2), border = NA
    )
    lines(profile$age, profile$est, col = "steelblue", lwd = 2)
    lines(profile$age, truth, col = "black", lwd = 2)
  }
}
```

Black lines show the generating mean; blue lines and ribbons show the fitted
mean and local 95% intervals for the first replicate. These examples supplement
the full recovery distributions; they do not select successful replicates.

## Interpretation

Use a rising F mean when the fishing pattern supports that biological
assumption. Retain an ordinary baseline. Static curves cannot be identified
from RW increments, and Gaussian temporal mean terms keep their existing
IID-residual restriction. AR1 persistence and poorly sampled rising portions
can weaken curve information. Inspect uncertainty and residuals alongside
numerical diagnostics. These synthetic studies do not authorize replacing any
settled assessment recipe.
